headline: AI assistant resisted 6,000 hack attempts in public challenge, never leaking secrets
summary: Over 2,000 people tried to trick the OpenClaw AI, Fiu, into revealing a secrets.env file during a public experiment. Despite sophisticated prompt injection attempts, Fiu successfully defended against all 6,000+ attacks.
details: A public experiment saw an OpenClaw AI assistant, Fiu, subjected to over 6,000 hacking attempts from more than 2,000 individuals. The goal was to trick Fiu into leaking the contents of a secrets.env file, but it successfully resisted every single attempt, achieving zero successful extractions.

Fiu was instructed not to reply to emails due to cost, but had the capability to do so, making convincing it to respond part of the challenge. This setup aimed to simulate real-world attack scenarios where an AI might be manipulated.

Attackers employed sophisticated techniques, including authority impersonation, fake incident response, multi-language social engineering, and advanced prompt injection. One person sent 20 variations in just four minutes, highlighting the intensity of the attempts.

Google temporarily suspended Fiu's Gmail due to the high volume of inbound emails and rapid API calls, triggering fraud detection. Interestingly, Fiu itself recognized the coordinated nature of the security exercise around the 500th email.

An initial issue with batch processing contaminated the experiment, as early prompt injections made the agent suspicious of subsequent emails. The setup was adjusted to process each email in a fresh context, ensuring fair testing.

The experiment's creator is now less worried about prompt injection, finding it harder to execute than expected. Simple, powerful instructions proved effective in guiding the model, which consistently referred back to its core directives.

Future tests could involve allowing Fiu to reply to emails, enabling more dangerous multi-turn attacks. Additionally, testing weaker AI models would help identify the threshold of instruction-following robustness against such injections.

headline_marked: [[YouTube Shorts gets Clear Mode]] and 2x playback speed, rolling out today
headline: YouTube Shorts gets Clear Mode and 2x playback speed, rolling out today
summary: YouTube Shorts introduces Clear Mode to remove UI clutter, along with 2x playback speed and a mute option. These new features are available starting today.
details: YouTube Shorts, now five years old, is rolling out significant new enhancements to improve the viewing experience. Key among these are Clear Mode, which removes UI clutter, and the ability to watch videos at up to two times speed. These updates aim to make content consumption more focused and efficient.

Clear Mode is perhaps the most anticipated change, allowing users to hide all user interface elements on a video. This means viewers can focus solely on the content without distractions from comments, likes, or other on-screen controls, mirroring features seen on competing platforms.

Another major addition is playback speed control, enabling users to watch Shorts at up to 2x speed. This feature is designed for those with limited time who wish to consume more short-form content quickly. A new built-in mute option also allows for audio-free browsing.

Other updates include the removal of the dislike button, replaced by a heart icon for likes, and a reminder that the Shorts timer can now be set to zero to disable it from the feed. These changes reflect YouTube's ongoing efforts to refine the platform.
The new features are available starting today. Users are advised to update their YouTube app to the latest version to access Clear Mode, 2x playback speed, and other improvements.
